missing: Provide the values of SLASHING_VETO_WINDOW and MIN_WITHDRAWAL_DELAY, or a test showing the redeem can complete during the veto window.
Provide a test demonstrating that finalizeSlashing transfers more than the applicable maxSlashablePercentageWad limit after the redeem.

reason: The cited code supports the earmark and balance-clamping behavior, but the report does not establish that the required timing is possible or demonstrate the resulting excess loss. The effect of slashing the DSS’s own shares on the claimed impact is also unclear.

evidence.claim: A DSS can inflate a vault's totalAssets before requestSlashing (by depositing and queuing a redeem), then withdraw its own funds during the veto window, so finalizeSlashing's earmarked amount exceeds remaining assets and slashAssets clamps to totalAssets(), slashing ~100% instead of maxSlashablePercentageWad.
evidence.support_reason: earmarkedStakes is fixed at request time from totalAssets() (SlasherLib.sol:86-90, 101-107) and reused verbatim at finalize (SlasherLib.sol:135-137). Vault.slashAssets clamps to Math.min(totalAssets(), totalAssetsToSlash) (Vault.sol:198) with no re-check against the DSS percentage. finishRedeem (Vault.sol:157-188) is permissionless and pays out during the veto window, so totalAssets can drop below the earmark. No check blocks the deposit/redeem/slash sequence.
preconditions: DSS is registered and operator is staked to it with the target vault (SlasherLib.sol:51)
DSS has capital to deposit into the vault and can wait MIN_WITHDRAWAL_DELAY before requestSlashing
DSS's own redeem finishes within SLASHING_VETO_WINDOW
missing_evidence: Confirmation that SLASHING_VETO_WINDOW >= MIN_WITHDRAWAL_DELAY so the DSS redeem can complete inside the veto window (Constants values not in provided source)
Test showing finalizeSlashing transfers ~totalAssets() after the DSS redeem, i.e. loss exceeds the maxSlashablePercentageWad bound
Whether the DSS's own shares are also burned/slashed proportionally, which would reduce net attacker gain
